title: Capacity contingency runbook - NA/EU/APAC
body:
Purpose

This runbook captures contingency plans, ETA commitments, and utilization scenarios for incremental GPU onboarding in NA / EU / APAC. It is intentionally operational and event-driven — use this when demand or supply variance causes our planned runway to slip and we need immediate mitigation or alternative routing.

Audience
- Infra on-call, capacity planners, SRE, on-prem delivery leads, sales engineering for large customers with Dedicated commitments.

Quick summary
- Current baseline procurement/onboarding plan is at-risk from supply delays in H100 inventory and slower cloud quota approvals in APAC.
- This document provides: an ETA matrix by cloud region + zone, three utilization scenarios (baseline / surge / degraded), explicit trigger thresholds, rapid actions by 24/72 hour windows, and fallbacks (cross-region routing, cheaper quantized variants, burst via spot pools).

Key assumptions (do not change without product/finance alignment)
- Primary target GPUs: H100-80GB for latency-sensitive and A100-80GB for throughput-heavy workloads.
- Baseline request growth: +18% month-over-month for hosted inference token volume for NA/EU; APAC growth assumed +25% MoM but from smaller base.
- Required headroom target: 35% available compute to meet 99th percentile latency SLOs after batching and caching.
- Quantization fallback degrades cost by ~30% but increases 99th pct latency by ~10–25% depending on prompt length.

ETA matrix (operational commitments)
- Table columns: region | cloud provider / zone | planned GPU type | planned add (units) | committed ETA | contingency ETA | expected util after add (p50)

NA | GCP-us-central1 | H100-80GB | 48 | 2026-04-12 | 2026-05-03 | 62%
NA | AWS-us-west-2 | A100-80GB | 96 | 2026-03-28 | 2026-04-18 | 58%
EU | GCP-europe-west4 | H100-80GB | 32 | 2026-04-19 | 2026-05-10 | 67%
EU | Azure-north-europe | A100-80GB | 48 | 2026-04-05 | 2026-04-26 | 60%
APAC | GCP-asia-southeast1 | A100-80GB | 40 | 2026-05-02 | 2026-05-23 | 54%
APAC | AWS-ap-northeast-1 | H100-80GB (partial) | 16 | 2026-05-12 | 2026-06-02 | 70%

Notes on ETA matrix: planned add is physical GPU cards equivalent at rack level (not instance counts). Committed ETA reflects vendor/provider committed delivery windows; contingency ETA adds a 3-week buffer for supply or quota delays. Expected utilization is modeled assuming automatic batching and KV prefix caching enabled for 75% of requests.

Utilization scenarios and operational impact
- Baseline (expected demand): p50 utilization after planned adds stays between 45–70% depending on region. No action required aside from normal autoscale.
- Surge (unexpected traffic +20–40% sustained over 72h): Triggers: sustained 95th percentile latency breach > SLO for 2 consecutive 1-hour windows AND utilization > 85% on primary region. Actions: enable cross-region routing (route 20–40% of requests to secondary region), enable quantized model variant for non-critical routes, expand spot pool burst +50% where cold-start acceptable.
- Degraded (supply shortfall causes >15% capacity loss vs plan): Triggers: failed provisioning for scheduled ETA beyond contingency ETA OR vendor cancellation. Actions: initiate emergency procurement (INFRA-2123), reseat burst policy to Dedicated customers, apply per-route throttles, prioritize traffic per customer SLAs, start customer comms template (sales-eng).

Trigger thresholds (operational)
- Green (no action): 95th pct latency < SLO AND region util < 75%
- Amber (prepare mitigation): 95th pct latency between SLO and SLO+20% OR region util 75–85% for >2h
- Red (execute contingency): 95th pct latency > SLO+20% for >30m OR region util >85% for >30m OR planned ETA missed beyond contingency ETA

24/72-hour action checklist (ordered)
- 0–24h: Verify metrics and alerts, spin up spot/ephemeral instances in target region, switch lightweight routes to quantized variants, notify oncall and sales-eng, open incident in incident-management and tag INFRA-2123.
- 24–72h: Activate cross-region routing policy via Smart Router (20–50% traffic shift depending on latency delta), enable long-tail KV cache reuse policies, apply temporary per-customer rate caps for non-SLA traffic, request expedited quota from cloud provider with support escalation.
- >72h: If still degraded, apply customer-tiered throttles (Dedicated > Enterprise > Free) and start formal customer communication plan. Begin vendor negotiation for next-available shipments or move to alternate GPU family if acceptable.

Fallbacks and decision logic (priorities)
1) Cross-region routing to same GPU family where possible (min latency delta goal: <15ms for critical routes)
2) Shift non-critical routes to quantized model variants (cost savings but higher latency)
3) Use spot/ephemeral capacity for batching-heavy workloads (not recommended for low-latency routes)
4) Customer-tier throttles and capacity reallocation

Risk register (brief)
- Vendor lead-time volatility: mitigated by secondary vendors and staggered PO schedule.
- Cloud quota approvals in APAC: mitigated by pre-approved quota templates and partner-managed accounts.
- Model compatibility with quantized kernels: keep a weekly compatibility sweep and avoid sudden global switches without canary.

Capacity delta quick reference (if contingency executed)
- Small (0–12 GPUs missing): quick patch — shift non-critical traffic to quantized and open spot pools. Estimated impact: latency +5–15% on affected routes.
- Medium (13–60 GPUs missing): execute cross-region routing + customer-tier throttles. Estimated impact: some customers downgraded to quantized variants, cost +8–14% as spot premiums used.
- Large (>60 GPUs missing): emergency procurement + contract fallback; prioritize Dedicated contractual obligations first. Customer comms mandatory.

Operational play examples (short)
- Example A (APAC quota delay): APAC expected add of 40 A100 delayed 3 weeks. Actions: apply 30% cross-region routing to NA EU, enable quantized fallback for 40% of chat traffic, expend spot capacity in ap-southeast to cover 20% of batch jobs. Result: latency SLOs maintained for critical customers; cost delta +12% for 3 weeks.
- Example B (H100 shipment shortfall in NA): Missing 60 H100 cards. Actions: reserve H100 capacity for top-10 Dedicated customers only, convert public hosted traffic to A100-quantized for low-priority routes, open vendor escalation and evaluate temporary GPU colo. Result: service for Dedicated customers preserved; increased latency on public hosted average +18%; customer comms initiated.

Monitoring and dashboards (immediate checks)
- Per-region 95th/99th latency, token/sec, GPU util by instance, canary request latency by route, cross-region failover rate.
- Owner for dashboards: Arjun Rao. Add runbook link to SRE playbook.

Open questions and notes
- Confirm finance approval for up to +18% spot budget burn for emergency bursts (Sophie to confirm by 2026-03-15).
- Confirm list of top-10 Dedicated customers tolerant to cross-region routing for customer-impact model.

Next steps (owners)
- Maya: finalize runbook, align with Product and Sales by 2026-03-16.
- Arjun: update dashboards and add amber/red automated runbook links by 2026-03-18.
- Liam: validate vendor secondary PO schedule and update procurement sheet by 2026-03-17.

Appendix (short)
- Contact list: SRE oncall channel #sre-oncall, procurement: procurement@redwood.com, sales-eng: sales-eng@redwood.com.
- Template incident message for customers and internal postmortem checklist attached in Confluence link above.

-- end runbook --
